ordered_diagnoses: Primary Adenocarcinoma of the Urinary Bladder

facts.raw_span: a 2-month history of intermittent painless hematuria with passage of clots
denied dysuria, frequency, or other lower urinary tract symptoms
no family history of malignancy
vital signs and abdominal and pelvic exams were unremarkable
hemoglobin level of 8.6 g/dL
serum creatinine and other biochemical parameters were within normal limits
a 2.9 × 2.5 × 2.4 cm polypoidal mass arising from the posterolateral wall of the bladder dome
both kidneys and the upper tracts appeared normal
Pre- and postvoid bladder volumes were 180 mL and 44 mL, respectively
an exophytic solid tumor measuring 1.5 × 2.0 cm on the anterior fundal wall, covered with slough
Histopathological analysis revealed an adenocarcinoma composed of mucinous and signet-ring cell components
a secondary adenocarcinoma or a rare variant of primary adenocarcinoma of the bladder was suspected

The patient presented with a 2-month history of intermittent painless hematuria, which is a key symptom of urinary tract disorders.
The patient had a low hemoglobin level, which is a common indicator of anemia.
The patient was found to have a polypoidal mass in the bladder, which was later diagnosed as adenocarcinoma.
The histopathological analysis revealed an adenocarcinoma composed of mucinous and signet-ring cell components.

concepts.preferred_label: Primary Adenocarcinoma of the Urinary Bladder
concepts.why: The patient's adenocarcinoma was suspected to be a rare variant of primary adenocarcinoma of the bladder.
The patient's adenocarcinoma was also suspected to be a secondary adenocarcinoma.
The patient had a high pre-void bladder volume and a low post-void bladder volume, which may indicate urinary tract obstruction.

rationales.F12: The suspicion of a secondary or primary adenocarcinoma of the bladder is based on the histopathological analysis.
